purpose.description: Evaluate identifiability when the system class is nonstationary and the interface must capture changing target-relevant structure over time.
purpose.role: Extend Interface Theory from fixed dynamical systems to evolving systems where observation requirements may change.
not_used_for: equating prediction under distribution shift with identifiability

system_class.description: Nonstationary systems with time-varying transition dynamics and evolving observation requirements.

target.description: Future target dependent on evolving system trajectory.

temporal_design_results.interpretation: Temporal adaptation provides no benefit when dynamics are invariant.
Tracking temporal change restores target purity.
Only adaptive interfaces preserve target-relevant distinctions.

temporal_frontier.finding: Required temporal access increases with nonstationarity.

relationship.description: Minimum interface cost as a function of environmental change rate.

failure_modes.name: temporal_stale_equivalence
failure_modes.description: Different current states share identical historical observations but have diverged dynamics.

failure_modes.name: regime_aliasing
failure_modes.description: Different system regimes produce identical observations under insufficient temporal resolution.

failure_modes.name: adaptation_lag
failure_modes.description: Interface update speed is slower than environmental change.

static_assumption.reason: The target mapping changes with system regime.

adaptive_factorization.condition: Interface includes sufficient temporal context or change detection.

decision.meaning: Nonstationarity converts interface design into a temporal adaptation problem.

notes: A stationary interface may become insufficient after distribution shift.
The correct resource is not historical data volume but preserved temporal distinctions.
Adaptive interfaces are required when the target-relevant structure itself changes.
